newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee called to open 1.00 cent lower.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee called to open 1.00 cent lower.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures were called to open 1.00 cents per lb lower on Monday, after top-grower Brazil got through the weekend frost-free, traders said.
Brazilian cooperative officials and coffee growers said they had not heard of any frosts on coffee farms by 1030 GMT on Monday.
Weather Services Corp. said on Monday temperatures cooled to "below to much below normal" in Brazil's coffee belt, but no damaging cold was observed.

Brazil's weather is expected to remain cold over the next couple of days, with low temperatures on Tuesday in the upper 30s and 40s (3-9 C). Wednesday's lows will range in the 40s F (5-9 C). No damaging cold is expected this week, WSC said.

Friday, New York arabica futures rose in relatively subdued dealings. July ended up 6.75 cents per lb, to 237.25 cents, after ranging between 238.50 and 228.00 cents. Second-month September ended 4.75 cents, to 214.15 cents, while the back months closed up 0.75 to 4.15.
The July/September spread widened to 23.10 cents today from 21.10 cents on Thursday.
Technically, traders said July would continue to run into some resistance at 240.00 cents, while support was seen at 233.00-232.00, then Thursday's low of 228.00 cents.
After Friday's close, the CSCE said certified coffee stocks fell by 1,650 60-kg bags as of June 5, to 43,625 bags, There were 3,115 bags pending grading, the exchange said.

The latest CFTC Commitment of Traders report released Friday showed non-commercial long positions in the two weeks ended June 3 fell by 1,316 lots, to 7,203 lots. Non-commercial short positions fell by 115 lots, to 1,647 lots.
Commercial long positions in the two weeks fell by 632 lots, to 7,118 lots, while commercial short positions fell by 2,363 lots to 16,483 lots.
Non-reportable long positions fell by 221 lots to 12,283 lots and non-reportable short positions rose by 309 lots, to 8,474 lots.
In London, robusta futures were firmer at midday Monday, but off early highs. LIFFE July rose $12 at the break, to $1,835, after peaking at $1,875. September was $20 higher, at $1,870.
